summary: Remove whitespace from the end while preserving indentation at the beginning.
documentation: trimEnd returns a new string after removing trailing JavaScript whitespace and line terminators. It leaves leading and interior characters intact, which matters for indented text records.
inputs: A string containing a single imported text record, possibly with trailing line breaks or spaces.
returns: The same text with trailing whitespace removed.
caution: This also removes trailing tabs, line breaks and nonbreaking spaces. It does not remove arbitrary punctuation, and it does not change the original string.
scenarios: Clean the end of an indented log line before displaying it.
Remove pasted line endings from an imported label while retaining its leading spaces.
Prepare fixed-layout text records where initial indentation carries meaning.
title: Clean a record without losing indentation
problem: Return the input with only its trailing whitespace removed. Preserve all leading indentation and interior whitespace. An all-whitespace input becomes an empty string.
hint: Call trimEnd on the string; trimming both ends would remove meaningful indentation.
goal: Use String.trimEnd() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
